video.title: Decisions: if, elif and else
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds. Code is typed out on a card, left to right in both languages. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Mr Okafor — the students’ science teacher (main character)
Mr Joseph — the students’ computer studies teacher (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice, talking to the student (warm, peer to peer)

scenes.narration: At the science museum, children under twelve pay half price. The ticket machine decides your price in a blink. That decision is an if.

A decision needs a question with a yes or no answer. Is age less than twelve? Python can compare with less than, greater than, two equals signs for the same, and exclamation equals for not the same. The answer is True or False.
An if line asks the question and ends with a colon. The lines under it are pushed in by four spaces, and they run only if the answer is True. Under else go the lines for False.
For more choices, add elif, short for else if. Under five, free. Under twelve, half price. Everyone else, full price. Python checks from the top and stops at the first True.
You can join questions with and and or. With and, both must be True. With or, one is enough. A free ticket if you are under five or over seventy.
Quick check! With that program, a girl who is exactly twelve buys a ticket. What does it print?
Full price. Twelve is not less than twelve. Mistakes like this hide at the edges, so always test the boundary: eleven, twelve and thirteen.
The most common bug: one equals sign stores, two equals signs compare. If you write if age equals twelve with one sign, Python stops with a syntax error. Inside an if, you almost always need two.
Decisions make programs smart. A quiz that says correct or try again. A game that ends when your lives reach zero. A phone that warns you when the battery is low.
In the app, open Logic gates. Try AND and OR with two switches, and watch when the lamp lights. Then solve the Door alarm: door or window open, and the alarm switched on.
Your turn. Age is fifteen. What is age greater than twelve, and age less than eighteen: True or False?
True. Remember: a comparison is True or False. if runs its indented lines only when True; else covers the rest; elif adds choices. Two equals signs compare. And test the boundaries.
Try it yourself: write a quiz with one question. If the answer is right, print Well done; else, print the right answer. Test it with a right answer and a wrong one.

checkpoints.prompt: Free under 5, half price under 12, else full price. A girl is exactly 12. What does it print?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — 12 is not less than 12, so she pays full price.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — less than 12 means 11 or under. At exactly 12, it’s full price.

checkpoints.prompt: age = 15. What is age > 12 and age < 18?
checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — both are True, and and needs both.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — 15 > 12 is True and 15 < 18 is True, so the whole thing is True.
